value.body: Actuaries use statistics, probability and finance to price and manage long-term financial risk — mainly in insurance, pensions and consulting. In India the profession is regulated by the Institute of Actuaries of India (IAI), a statutory body under the Actuaries Act, 2006. It is a professional qualification built from a series of exams, not a single degree, and a B.Sc in mathematics or statistics is a common starting point.

items.label: Regulator
items.note: Statutory body under the Actuaries Act, 2006

items.label: Entry test
items.note: Actuarial Common Entrance Test; passing it allows student membership of IAI

items.label: Exam stages
items.value: Core Principles → Core Practices → Specialist Principles → Specialist Advanced

items.label: ACET result validity
items.source: As reported (Careers360), based on IAI rules

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Register with IAI and pass ACET (eligibility has been Class 12 pass or equivalent; check the current rule on the IAI site). After ACET you enrol as a student member and take the professional papers one by one. There is no college admission involved; many people study for the papers while doing a degree or working.

value.title: At a glance
items: Qualification usually takes several years of exams, often written alongside a full-time job.
Pass rates in the professional papers are modest, so repeat attempts are common.
Work is mostly in life and general insurers, reinsurers, pension and benefits consulting, and analytics teams.
Exam fees are paid per paper, so the total cost depends on how many attempts you need.
